normalQuestions.learningObjective: Given a scenario, analyze vulnerabilities and attacks, and recommend solutions to reduce the attack surface.
normalQuestions.stem: A web service in a cloud environment fetches URLs supplied by users. Which items best separate a defensible answer from a superficial one? (Select all that apply.)

choices.A: Validate URLs
choices.B: Deny metadata endpoints
choices.C: Restrict egress
choices.D: Verify package provenance
choices.E: Test tenant isolation

The defense controls where the server may connect: validate the URL before fetching (A), block access to metadata endpoints (B), and restrict outbound egress (C). Verifying package provenance and testing tenant isolation defend the supply chain and authorization, not the fetch path.

whyWrong.D: Verifying package provenance defends the build pipeline, not runtime URL fetching.
whyWrong.E: Testing tenant isolation addresses authorization flaws, not SSRF.

normalQuestions.learningObjective: Given a scenario, integrate appropriate controls in the design of a secure architecture.
normalQuestions.stem: A platform team is defining the minimum evidence package for a high-risk workflow. An earlier shortcut failed because partner APIs accept transactions from multiple external organizations. Which option is most defensible after weighing security value, operational burden, and evidence quality?

choices.A: Limit scopes, review vendor controls, monitor activity, define revocation, and validate least-privilege integration design
choices.B: Define trust boundaries, routing, identity, logging, and encryption consistently across hybrid paths
choices.C: Classify data and combine DLP, access control, encryption, monitoring, and exception handling
choices.D: Map controls to threats, expected outcomes, telemetry, tests, owners, and failure conditions
choices.E: Use strong partner identity, per-partner authorization, schema validation, rate limits, replay protection, and signed audit records

With many external organizations transacting, option E fits directly, distinguishing each partner, validating payloads, and producing tamper-evident records. Vendor integration controls, hybrid boundaries, DLP, and control-to-threat mapping address other scenarios, not the multi-partner API surface.

whyWrong.A: Vendor/third-party integration controls address delegated authorization and data movement and can cover multiple partners, but they are less complete than E for securing this transactional partner-API surface.
whyWrong.B: Hybrid trust-boundary controls address connectivity paths, not partner transactions.
whyWrong.C: DLP protects data movement, not per-partner API authorization and validation.
whyWrong.D: Control-to-threat mapping is documentation, not the runtime API control set needed.

sources: CAS005 LO 2.3: Given a scenario, integrate appropriate controls in the design of a secure architecture.

whyWrong.C: Device segmentation fits unsupported clinical systems, not granting controlled vendor access.
whyWrong.D: Engineering-function isolation fits a logic-editing workstation, not remote vendor support.
whyWrong.E: Legacy-protocol containment fits legacy protocol flows, not remote access sessions.

normalQuestions.stem: Developers copied production customer records into a shared test environment to troubleshoot faster. Which target-state design is the most complete and defensible?

choices.A: Use a procedure that turns the policy into required steps, evidence, approvals, and tests
choices.B: Use GRC tooling or an evidence register mapping controls, owners, exceptions, tests, and obligations
choices.C: Require change governance: risk classification, emergency approval, rollback evidence, and post-change review
choices.D: Build a RACI separating recommendation, consultation, approval, execution, and evidence ownership
choices.E: Apply data governance to staging: minimization, masking/tokenization, access limits, and retention

normalQuestions.explanation: Nonproduction environments still inherit data-protection obligations. The complete design applies data governance to staging, minimizing data, masking or tokenizing sensitive fields, limiting access, and setting retention (E). Those measures are exactly what protects the copied customer records.

whyWrong.A: A procedure documents how to act but does not itself protect the data in the test environment.
whyWrong.B: A GRC register tracks evidence; it does not minimize or mask the copied records.
whyWrong.C: Change governance handles changes, not the data-protection gap in staging.
whyWrong.D: A RACI clarifies ownership but does not implement the data safeguards needed here.

whyCorrect.E: Directly protects the regulated data in staging through minimization, masking, access limits, and retention.

choices.D: Log suspicious access
choices.E: Test tenant isolation

The fix enforces authorization on each object (C), logs suspicious access for detection (D), and tests tenant isolation to prove the boundary holds (E). Monitoring dependency changes and exploit attempts addresses supply-chain and exploitation risks, not access control.

whyWrong.A: Monitoring dependency changes addresses supply-chain risk, not authorization.
whyWrong.B: Monitoring exploit attempts fits exploitation-aware prioritization, not access control.

sources: CAS005 LO 4.2: Given a scenario, analyze vulnerabilities and attacks, and recommend solutions to reduce the attack surface.

whyCorrect.C: Authorizing per object stops one user from reading another tenant's records.
whyCorrect.D: Logging suspicious access detects attempts to abuse object identifiers.

normalQuestions.stem: A SIEM receives identity, EDR, DNS, and cloud logs, but its alerts are noisy and disconnected. The team already bought tooling, but this issue is unresolved. Which option best names the control objective the reviewer should apply?

choices.B: Normalize and correlate events with asset, identity, threat, and response context
choices.C: Track coverage, fidelity, false positives, time to detect, time to respond, and unresolved high-risk gaps
choices.D: Monitor cloud audit events, identity changes, network control changes, and anomalous API use
choices.E: Use behavior baselines with risk scoring, peer comparison, and triage context

The objective is to normalize the data and correlate events with asset, identity, threat, and response context so each alert becomes decision-useful (B). The other options add detection sources or metrics but do not turn noisy, disconnected logs into correlated, actionable findings.

whyWrong.A: Aggregating into timelines targets staged weak-signal attacks, not general alert correlation.
whyWrong.C: Metrics measure detection performance, not alert correlation.
whyWrong.D: Cloud control-plane monitoring is one source, not the cross-source correlation needed.
whyWrong.E: Behavioral baselines flag unusual activity, not the broad correlation this requires.

normalQuestions.learningObjective: Given a scenario, integrate appropriate controls in the design of a secure architecture.
normalQuestions.stem: A compliance lead questions whether the proposed control can be tested in operation. The business accepts the goal, but the reviewer must address that an on-prem application calls cloud services over multiple private and public paths. What should the security practitioner recommend FIRST?

choices.A: Define trust boundaries, routing, identity, logging, and encryption consistently across hybrid paths
choices.B: Limit scopes, review vendor controls, monitor activity, define revocation, and validate least-privilege integration design
choices.C: Classify data and combine DLP, access control, encryption, monitoring, and exception handling
choices.D: Map controls to threats, expected outcomes, telemetry, tests, owners, and failure conditions
choices.E: Use strong partner identity, per-partner authorization, schema validation, rate limits, replay protection, and signed audit records

normalQuestions.explanation: Hybrid security breaks down when control assumptions differ between on-prem and cloud. With an app reaching cloud services over multiple private and public paths, the first step is to define consistent trust boundaries, routing, identity, logging, and encryption across all those hybrid paths (A). Vendor integration, DLP, control-to-threat mapping, and partner-API controls each fit other scenarios and do not map the hybrid connectivity here.

whyWrong.B: Vendor integration controls fit a SaaS plugin, not hybrid connectivity between on-prem and cloud.
whyWrong.C: DLP protects data movement, not the trust-boundary consistency across mixed paths.
whyWrong.D: Control-to-threat mapping is documentation, not the hybrid boundary design needed first.
whyWrong.E: Partner-API controls fit many external organizations, not one app crossing private and public paths.

sources: CAS005 LO 2.3: Given a scenario, integrate appropriate controls in the design of a secure architecture.

whyCorrect.A: Defining consistent trust boundaries, routing, identity, logging, and encryption across hybrid paths closes the cross-environment gap.

normalQuestions.learningObjective: Given a scenario, analyze data to enable monitoring and response activities.
normalQuestions.stem: Individual low-severity events look normal on their own but together show staged exfiltration. A compliance lead asks whether the proposed control can be tested in operation. What should the practitioner recommend FIRST?

choices.A: Normalize and correlate events with asset, identity, threat, and response context
choices.B: Monitor cloud audit events, identity changes, network control changes, and anomalous API use
choices.C: Use behavior baselines with risk scoring, peer comparison, and triage context
choices.D: Track coverage, fidelity, false positives, time to detect, time to respond, and unresolved high-risk gaps
choices.E: Aggregate endpoint, network, identity, and data-movement signals into a timeline and detection

normalQuestions.explanation: Sophisticated attacks hide as separate weak signals that only reveal intent when combined. Aggregate data analysis brings endpoint, network, identity, and data-movement signals into one timeline so the staged exfiltration becomes a single detectable pattern (E). The other options are useful monitoring capabilities but do not stitch the weak signals together as this scenario needs.

whyWrong.A: Correlation with context is related but broader; the decisive need is joining signals into a timeline.
whyWrong.B: Cloud control-plane monitoring is one source, not the cross-domain aggregation needed.
whyWrong.C: Behavioral baselines flag unusual activity but do not assemble the multi-step story.
whyWrong.D: Metrics measure detection performance, not the act of connecting weak signals.

normalQuestions.learningObjective: Given a scenario, apply the appropriate cryptographic use case and/or technique.
normalQuestions.stem: A risk owner asks which control proves the organization understood the constraints. Auditors want proof for a finding that audit records must resist alteration by administrators after privileged actions. Which evidence would let a reviewer defend the decision against weaker alternatives? (Select all that apply.)

choices.A: Separate admins
choices.B: Verify integrity
choices.C: Limit detokenization
choices.D: Use unique salts
choices.E: Protect log writes

normalQuestions.explanation: Audit records that must resist insider alteration need tamper-resistant, append-only logging with independent oversight. Separating admins enforces separation of duties so no one person can both act and erase evidence, verifying integrity detects any change, and protecting log writes makes records append-only. Detokenization limits and password salts solve unrelated cryptographic problems.

whyWrong.C: Limiting detokenization fits reversible tokenization, not tamper-resistant logging.
whyWrong.D: Unique salts fit password hashing, not audit-record integrity.

sources: CAS005 LO 3.8: Given a scenario, apply the appropriate cryptographic use case and/or technique.

whyCorrect.A: Separating admins enforces separation of duties so the actor cannot also alter the log.
whyCorrect.B: Verifying integrity detects any tampering with stored audit records.
whyCorrect.E: Protecting log writes makes records append-only and resistant to administrator edits.

normalQuestions.learningObjective: Given a scenario, perform threat modeling activities.
normalQuestions.topic: assets, data flows, trust boundaries, and assumptions
normalQuestions.stem: A post-incident review asks security to separate the true cause from convenient symptoms. In this scenario, a payments API accepts customer records, calls a fraud service, and writes decisions back to core systems. Which option best names the control objective the reviewer should apply?

choices.A: Profile threats against the organization's real assets, exposure, controls, and processes
choices.B: Map the attack chain to preventive, detective, and responsive controls across phases
choices.C: Model AI risks: prompt injection, retrieval leakage, tool misuse, data poisoning, output trust, and approval limits
choices.D: Enumerate the attack surface: external, internal, identity, data, and supply-chain exposure
choices.E: Model assets, actors, data flows, trust boundaries, dependencies, and assumptions before choosing controls

normalQuestions.explanation: Threat modeling begins by defining what is being modeled. For a payments API spanning customer data, a fraud service, and core systems, the control objective is to model the assets, actors, data flows, trust boundaries, and assumptions first (E). Identifying actors and data stores and recording assumptions makes the model auditable.

whyWrong.A: Threat profiling weighs which threats apply, after the system model.
whyWrong.B: Kill-chain control placement comes once boundaries and flows are known.
whyWrong.C: AI threat modeling does not fit this conventional API.
whyWrong.D: Attack-surface enumeration lists exposure but does not draw trust boundaries first.

normalQuestions.learningObjective: Given a scenario, implement security in the early stages of the systems life cycle and throughout subsequent stages.
normalQuestions.stem: A security operations manager is turning lessons learned into durable control requirements. Tooling is already purchased, but the unresolved issue is that the team relies on a single annual penetration test for a rapidly changing API. Which controls or evidence should be included? (Select all that apply.)

choices.A: Scan dependencies
choices.B: Document custody
choices.C: Verify provenance
choices.D: Gate high-risk findings
choices.E: Test APIs

normalQuestions.explanation: Assurance must match the development cadence and risk; one annual test cannot keep up with a fast-changing API. The fix layers continuous testing into the pipeline: scan dependencies for known issues (A), gate releases on high-risk findings (D), and test the APIs continuously (E). Documenting custody (B) and verifying provenance (C) belong to supply-chain assurance, not software test layering.

whyWrong.B: Documenting custody is a supply-chain control, not part of ongoing software testing.
whyWrong.C: Verifying provenance fits hardware or component sourcing, not API test cadence.

sources: CAS005 LO 2.2: Given a scenario, implement security in the early stages of the systems life cycle and throughout subsequent stages.

whyCorrect.A: Scanning dependencies surfaces known vulnerabilities continuously instead of once a year.
whyCorrect.D: Gating high-risk findings prevents risky changes from shipping between tests.
whyCorrect.E: Continuous API testing matches assurance to the API's rapid change rate.

normalQuestions.learningObjective: Given a scenario, analyze data and artifacts in support of incident response activities.
normalQuestions.stem: Operations wants to rebuild a compromised server, but its active connections, process memory, and cloud tokens may still reveal the attack's scope. The business accepts the goal; the reviewer must respond. Which option best names the control objective the reviewer should apply?

choices.A: Normalize timestamps, preserve source context, and build a cross-source event timeline
choices.B: Preserve host artifacts, collect memory/disk evidence, hash samples, and analyze behavior safely
choices.C: Preserve volatile and cloud/session evidence where feasible while coordinating containment and recovery
choices.D: Combine recovery validation with root-cause remediation, detection updates, and lessons learned
choices.E: Analyze workload identity, runtime telemetry, cloud audit logs, data access, and insider-threat context

normalQuestions.explanation: A rebuild erases perishable evidence such as live connections, memory, and cloud tokens that reveal the attack's reach. The objective is to preserve that volatile and cloud/session evidence while still coordinating containment and recovery (C). The other options are valid IR steps but do not protect the perishable evidence the rebuild would destroy.

whyWrong.A: Timeline reconstruction supports analysis but does not capture perishable evidence first.
whyWrong.B: Host/malware forensics follows a nearby lesson thread but does not record the active connections this pre-rebuild scenario requires.
whyWrong.D: Recovery validation comes after the volatile evidence is secured.
whyWrong.E: Workload-identity analysis suits abnormal cloud identity use, not pre-rebuild preservation.

sources: CAS005 LO 4.4: Given a scenario, analyze data and artifacts in support of incident response activities.

whyCorrect.C: Preserving volatile and session evidence before rebuild keeps the scope and root cause recoverable.

normalQuestions.learningObjective: Given a scenario, analyze requirements to design resilient systems.
normalQuestions.stem: An architecture board is comparing controls that look similar on a checklist. Tooling is already purchased, but the unresolved issue is that a failover plan can restore service quickly yet may replay duplicate transactions. Which items best distinguish a defensible answer from a superficial one? (Select all that apply.)

choices.A: Maintain spares
choices.B: Test reconciliation
choices.C: Enforce idempotent processing
choices.D: Map dependencies
choices.E: Monitor duplicate events

normalQuestions.explanation: Availability without integrity can cause business and security failure; fast failover that replays duplicate transactions corrupts data. The defensible set protects integrity during recovery: enforce idempotent processing so replays do no harm (C), test reconciliation to catch mismatches (B), and monitor for duplicate events (E). Maintaining spares (A) and mapping dependencies (D) help availability but do not prevent duplicate-transaction corruption.

whyWrong.A: Maintaining spares supports availability, not transaction integrity during failover.
whyWrong.D: Mapping dependencies supports recovery planning, not preventing duplicate transactions.

sources: CAS005 LO 2.1: Given a scenario, analyze requirements to design resilient systems.

whyCorrect.B: Testing reconciliation detects and resolves the data mismatches duplicate transactions create.
whyCorrect.C: Idempotent processing ensures replayed transactions produce no duplicate effect.
whyCorrect.E: Monitoring duplicate events surfaces replay problems before they corrupt data.

normalQuestions.learningObjective: Explain how compliance affects information security strategies.
normalQuestions.stem: A healthcare analytics workflow touches patient data, billing metadata, and operational dashboards. Which items make an industry-compliance answer defensible rather than superficial? (Select all that apply.)

choices.A: Restrict minimum necessary access
choices.B: Validate permitted use
choices.C: Show residual risk trends
choices.D: Verify period of coverage
choices.E: Retain audit evidence

normalQuestions.explanation: Healthcare data brings sector-specific duties. A defensible strategy restricts access to the minimum necessary (A), validates that each use is permitted (B), and retains audit evidence to prove compliance (E). Residual-risk trends and attestation coverage belong to reporting and audit-evidence topics instead.

whyWrong.C: Residual risk trends are executive-reporting evidence, not sector compliance controls.
whyWrong.D: Verifying period of coverage relates to assurance artifacts, not healthcare data handling.

sources: CAS005 LO 1.3: Explain how compliance affects information security strategies.

whyCorrect.A: Minimum-necessary access is a core healthcare data-handling requirement.
whyCorrect.B: Validating permitted use ensures patient data is processed only for allowed purposes.
whyCorrect.E: Retained audit evidence demonstrates the sector obligations were met.

normalQuestions.learningObjective: Given a scenario, analyze data and artifacts in support of incident response activities.
normalQuestions.stem: A production incident exposed a weakness previously treated as an acceptable shortcut. The control debate begins after auditors ask for proof that restored files are clean, but the same root cause can reintroduce compromise. Which finding is the most important root cause to address?

choices.A: Analyze workload identity, runtime telemetry, cloud audit logs, data access, and insider-threat context
choices.B: Preserve host artifacts, collect memory/disk evidence, hash samples, and analyze behavior safely
choices.C: Combine recovery validation with root-cause remediation, detection updates, and lessons learned
choices.D: Normalize timestamps, preserve source context, and build a cross-source event timeline
choices.E: Preserve volatile and cloud/session evidence where feasible while coordinating containment and recovery

normalQuestions.explanation: A clean restore is not full recovery while the original weakness survives. Recovery and continuous improvement validates the restore, remediates the root cause, updates detections, and records lessons learned (C). The other options are valid IR activities from earlier phases but do not close the reinfection gap.

whyWrong.A: Workload-identity analysis suits abnormal cloud identity use, not recovery validation.
whyWrong.B: Host/malware forensics fits a self-deleting binary, not a clean-restore check.
whyWrong.D: Timeline reconstruction supports analysis, not closing the reinfection path.
whyWrong.E: Volatile-evidence preservation happens before rebuild, not in recovery.

sources: CAS005 LO 4.4: Given a scenario, analyze data and artifacts in support of incident response activities.

whyCorrect.C: Validating the restore plus root-cause remediation and detection updates prevents the compromise from recurring.

normalQuestions.learningObjective: Given a scenario, analyze requirements to design resilient systems.
normalQuestions.stem: A production incident exposes a weakness that had been treated as an acceptable shortcut. Engineering could implement several controls, but the constraint stands: a load-balanced service still fails when a shared identity provider and shared storage tier are unavailable. Which finding is the most important root cause to address?

choices.A: Design redundancy, segmentation, passive monitoring, spare strategy, and documented recovery procedures
choices.B: Include brokers, queues, identity, DNS, secrets, and external dependencies in recovery testing
choices.C: Require dependency mapping, replication design, and tested failover/restore evidence aligned to RTO and RPO
choices.D: Design recovery to preserve transaction integrity, idempotency, ordering, and reconciliation
choices.E: Identify shared failure domains and remove or mitigate single points across dependencies

normalQuestions.explanation: Running many nodes does not remove common dependencies; the load-balanced service still shares one identity provider and one storage tier. The root cause is the shared failure domain, so the answer identifies those single points across dependencies and removes or mitigates them (E). Redundancy design, broad recovery testing, RTO/RPO evidence, and transaction integrity each address neighboring concerns but not the hidden common dependency that takes the whole service down.

whyWrong.A: Redundancy and procedures suit specialized components, not finding the hidden common dependency here.
whyWrong.B: Recovery testing helps verify, but the root cause is the shared single points themselves.
whyWrong.C: RTO/RPO evidence proves recovery targets, not the existence of a shared failure domain.
whyWrong.D: Transaction-integrity recovery preserves correctness, not availability against shared dependencies.

sources: CAS005 LO 2.1: Given a scenario, analyze requirements to design resilient systems.

whyCorrect.E: Identifying and mitigating shared failure domains removes the single points (shared IdP and storage) that defeat the load balancing.

normalQuestions.learningObjective: Given a scenario, analyze data to enable monitoring and response activities.
normalQuestions.stem: A SOC reports alert counts but cannot explain its detection quality or response outcomes. The team already bought tooling, but this issue is unresolved. Which elements belong in the design package? (Select all that apply.)

choices.A: Correlate data movement
choices.B: Measure response time
choices.C: Normalize fields
choices.D: Measure detection coverage
choices.E: Track false positives

normalQuestions.explanation: Alert counts do not show whether detection works. Monitoring metrics make performance measurable: measure response time (B), measure detection coverage (D), and track false positives (E). Correlating data movement and normalizing fields support correlation rather than measure how well detection and response perform.

whyWrong.A: Correlating data movement supports correlation, not measuring SOC performance.
whyWrong.C: Normalizing fields supports correlation, not measuring SOC outcomes.

sources: CAS005 LO 4.1: Given a scenario, analyze data to enable monitoring and response activities.

whyCorrect.B: Measuring response time shows how quickly the SOC acts after detection.
whyCorrect.D: Measuring detection coverage shows what the SOC can and cannot see.
whyCorrect.E: Tracking false positives shows alert fidelity, not just volume.

normalQuestions.learningObjective: Given a scenario, apply security concepts to the design of access, authentication, and authorization systems.
normalQuestions.stem: A third-party integration review needs a decision before production credentials are issued. Administrators use standing privileges across production and cloud consoles. Which controls or evidence should be included? (Select all that apply.)

choices.A: Review break-glass use
choices.B: Use SCIM or lifecycle automation
choices.C: Step up authentication
choices.D: Time-bound elevation
choices.E: Record admin sessions

normalQuestions.explanation: Standing privilege widens the blast radius and weakens accountability, so administration should be just-in-time and auditable. A PAM/JIT design grants access only when needed, with time-bound elevation (D), recorded admin sessions (E), and reviewed break-glass use (A). SCIM/lifecycle automation (B) handles account provisioning, and step-up authentication (C) raises factor assurance, but neither removes standing privilege.

whyWrong.B: SCIM/lifecycle automation provisions accounts; it does not eliminate standing admin privilege.
whyWrong.C: Step-up authentication strengthens login assurance, not the duration of privilege.

sources: CAS005 LO 2.4: Given a scenario, apply security concepts to the design of access, authentication, and authorization systems.

whyCorrect.A: Reviewing break-glass use ensures emergency access is rare, justified, and audited.
whyCorrect.D: Time-bound elevation replaces standing privilege with access that expires automatically.
whyCorrect.E: Recording admin sessions provides the accountability standing access lacks.

normalQuestions.learningObjective: Given a scenario, troubleshoot complex network infrastructure security issues.
normalQuestions.stem: A platform owner asks for the fastest path, but security needs a durable design. Auditors want proof for a finding that authentication and DNS services degrade during a burst while the network links remain under capacity. Which target-state design is most complete and defensible?

choices.A: Trace routing and enforcement paths to close inspection and logging gaps for lateral traffic
choices.B: Inspect DNS telemetry, resolver policy, domain reputation, and DNS security controls
choices.C: Compare TLS versions, cipher suites, certificate chain trust, mTLS requirements, and proxy bypass rules
choices.D: Validate SPF, DKIM, DMARC alignment, enforcement policy, and partner sending paths
choices.E: Investigate rate limits, service capacity, caching, failover, and control-plane dependencies

normalQuestions.explanation: Because the links are not saturated, this is service-level resource exhaustion, not bandwidth. The durable design investigates rate limits, service capacity, caching, failover, and control-plane dependencies to find and relieve the real bottleneck. The routing, DNS, TLS, and email options solve neighboring problems that do not explain the burst-time degradation.

whyWrong.A: Routing-path tracing fits lateral-traffic blind spots, not service saturation.
whyWrong.B: DNS-detection telemetry fits malicious-domain hunting, not capacity-driven degradation.
whyWrong.C: TLS comparison fits inspection mismatches, not resource exhaustion.
whyWrong.D: Email authentication validation fits spoofing, not service capacity.

sources: CAS005 LO 3.3: Given a scenario, troubleshoot complex network infrastructure security issues.

whyCorrect.E: Examining service capacity, rate limits, and failover targets the actual saturation, since the links are not the limit.

normalQuestions.learningObjective: Given a scenario, securely implement cloud capabilities in an enterprise environment.
normalQuestions.stem: A security engineer must choose between two controls that are each valid in a different context. The debate started when auditors asked for proof, since cloud workloads run containers and functions with broad runtime permissions and unknown dependencies. Which finding is the most important root cause to address?

choices.A: Harden images/functions with least privilege, dependency scanning, signed artifacts, secret isolation, and runtime monitoring
choices.B: Define approved connectivity, segmentation, encryption, routing, and monitoring for each data path
choices.C: Build landing-zone guardrails for identity, logging, encryption, network segmentation, tagging, and policy-as-code
choices.D: Use centralized key-management patterns with ownership, rotation, separation of duties, logging, and envelope encryption where appropriate
choices.E: Use discovery, risk assessment, sanctioned alternatives, access controls, and monitoring rather than blind blocking only

normalQuestions.explanation: Cloud-native workload risk spans both the supply chain and runtime identity. Broad runtime permissions plus unknown dependencies point straight to workload hardening: least privilege, dependency scanning, signed artifacts, secret isolation, and runtime monitoring (A). Per-path connectivity, landing-zone guardrails, key management, and shadow-IT discovery each address neighboring topics, not the container/function workload itself.

whyWrong.B: Per-path connectivity controls address data flow, not workload permissions and dependencies.
whyWrong.C: Landing-zone guardrails set account baselines, not per-workload runtime hardening.
whyWrong.D: Key management governs keys, not container/function runtime identity.
whyWrong.E: Shadow-IT discovery targets unsanctioned SaaS, not cloud-native workload risk.

sources: CAS005 LO 2.5: Given a scenario, securely implement cloud capabilities in an enterprise environment.

whyCorrect.A: Hardening images and functions with least privilege, dependency scanning, signed artifacts, secret isolation, and runtime monitoring directly addresses broad runtime permissions and unknown dependencies.

normalQuestions.learningObjective: Given a scenario, integrate Zero Trust concepts into system architecture design.
normalQuestions.stem: A service team proposes buying a tool, but the reviewer wants a control objective defined first. An earlier shortcut failed because a VPN grants broad access for eight hours after login, regardless of device or session risk. Which option best names the control objective the reviewer should apply?

choices.A: Use continuous, context-aware authorization with least-privilege access to specific resources
choices.B: Validate service identity, authorization, input, and context at API boundaries
choices.C: Require asset identity, posture checks, and attestation before granting sensitive access
choices.D: Place enforcement points close to protected resources and test bypass paths
choices.E: Create resource-level boundaries with explicit policy, microsegmentation, and monitored service-to-service access

normalQuestions.explanation: Zero Trust is a decision system, not a trusted network tunnel; a VPN that grants eight hours of broad access ignores changing device and session risk. The objective is continuous, context-aware authorization that grants least-privilege access to specific resources and re-evaluates risk (A). API validation, device attestation, PEP placement, and microsegmentation each address a different problem and do not replace the implicit-trust VPN model.

whyWrong.B: API-boundary validation verifies calls, not the broad time-based VPN trust.
whyWrong.C: Device attestation gates access at sign-in, but does not provide continuous re-evaluation.
whyWrong.D: PEP placement fixes portal-only enforcement, not standing VPN access duration.
whyWrong.E: Microsegmentation limits lateral movement, not the implicit-trust VPN session model.

sources: CAS005 LO 2.6: Given a scenario, integrate Zero Trust concepts into system architecture design.

whyCorrect.A: Continuous, context-aware, least-privilege authorization re-evaluates risk instead of granting broad standing VPN access.

normalQuestions.learningObjective: Given a scenario, analyze data and artifacts in support of incident response activities.
normalQuestions.stem: A suspicious binary disabled defenses and then deleted itself, and auditors want proof of how it was handled. Which items best separate a defensible answer from a superficial one? (Select all that apply.)

choices.A: Collect artifacts
choices.B: Use isolated analysis
choices.C: Update detections
choices.D: Hash samples
choices.E: Record source clocks

normalQuestions.explanation: A self-deleting binary destroys evidence, so malware and forensic analysis must preserve and handle what remains carefully. Collect the available artifacts (A), study them in an isolated environment (B), and hash samples to record and verify their integrity (D). Updating detections is a later improvement, and recording source clocks belongs to timeline reconstruction, not forensic handling here.

whyWrong.C: Updating detections is a continuous-improvement step, not part of preserving and analyzing the sample.
whyWrong.E: Recording source clocks supports cross-source timelines, not malware sample handling.

sources: CAS005 LO 4.4: Given a scenario, analyze data and artifacts in support of incident response activities.

whyCorrect.A: Collecting available artifacts preserves the evidence the self-deleting binary tries to erase.
whyCorrect.B: Isolated analysis studies malware behavior without endangering production.
whyCorrect.D: Hashing samples records and lets analysts verify their integrity so findings stay verifiable and shareable.

normalQuestions.learningObjective: Given a scenario, securely implement cloud capabilities in an enterprise environment.
normalQuestions.stem: A risk owner asks which control proves the team understood the scenario constraints. Tooling is already purchased, but the unresolved issue is that private circuits, VPNs, and public endpoints all reach the same cloud data platform. Which evidence points would let a reviewer defend the decision against plausible alternatives? (Select all that apply.)

choices.A: Monitor transfer activity
choices.B: Map ingress and egress
choices.C: Segment access paths
choices.D: Centralize control-plane logs
choices.E: Enforce encryption policy

normalQuestions.explanation: Secure cloud adoption requires explicit control over connectivity and data flow when many path types reach one platform. The defensible evidence maps ingress and egress (B), segments the access paths (C), and monitors transfer activity (A). Centralizing control-plane logs (D) and enforcing encryption policy (E) are landing-zone baseline controls, not the path-level connectivity governance this scenario asks for.

whyWrong.D: Centralizing control-plane logs is a landing-zone guardrail, not per-path connectivity evidence.
whyWrong.E: Enforcing encryption policy is a baseline guardrail, not the connectivity governance asked for here.

normalQuestions.learningObjective: Given a scenario, implement hardware security technologies and techniques.
normalQuestions.stem: A security council is deciding which evidence to require before approval. Auditors want proof for a finding that edge devices receive firmware from a field update service over unreliable networks. Which items best separate a defensible answer from a superficial one? (Select all that apply.)

choices.A: Collect attestation
choices.B: Verify signatures
choices.C: Prevent rollback
choices.D: Centralize key custody
choices.E: Authenticate devices

normalQuestions.explanation: Firmware delivered over an unreliable network must be provably genuine and current. Verifying signatures confirms authenticity, preventing rollback blocks downgrade to a vulnerable build, and authenticating devices ensures only known endpoints participate.

whyWrong.A: Attestation provides boot-integrity evidence, a different property than signed-firmware delivery.
whyWrong.D: Centralizing key custody fits HSM signing-key protection, not field firmware integrity.

sources: CAS005 LO 3.4: Given a scenario, implement hardware security technologies and techniques.

whyCorrect.B: Verifying signatures proves the delivered firmware is authentic and unaltered.
whyCorrect.C: Preventing rollback stops attackers forcing an older, vulnerable firmware version.
whyCorrect.E: Authenticating devices ensures only trusted endpoints accept the update.

normalQuestions.learningObjective: Explain the importance of advanced cryptographic concepts.
normalQuestions.stem: A program owner needs a recommendation defensible to legal, audit, and engineering. Engineering can implement several controls, but the constraint stands: business units want joint analytics without revealing their raw datasets to each other. Which elements belong in the design package? (Select all that apply.)

choices.A: Protect keys and outputs
choices.B: Evaluate performance
choices.C: Prioritize long-lived data
choices.D: Inventory algorithms
choices.E: Validate legal fit

normalQuestions.explanation: Computing on shared data without exposing the raw inputs points to privacy-preserving computation such as homomorphic encryption or SMPC, but those techniques carry real cost and limits. Protecting keys and outputs preserves confidentiality, evaluating performance checks the heavy compute overhead is acceptable, and validating legal fit confirms the approach satisfies privacy obligations.

whyWrong.C: Prioritizing long-lived data fits post-quantum planning, not privacy-preserving analytics.
whyWrong.D: Inventorying algorithms fits crypto-agility planning, not this HE/SMPC decision.

sources: CAS005 LO 3.7: Explain the importance of advanced cryptographic concepts.

whyCorrect.A: Protecting keys and outputs keeps the privacy-preserving computation confidential end to end.
whyCorrect.B: Evaluating performance confirms the heavy compute cost of HE/SMPC is workable.
whyCorrect.E: Validating legal fit ensures the joint-analytics design meets privacy and regulatory limits.

normalQuestions.learningObjective: Given a scenario, analyze requirements to enhance the security of endpoints and servers.
normalQuestions.stem: A platform team is designing the minimum evidence package for a high-risk workflow. Auditors want proof for a finding that servers frequently lose endpoint telemetry after local-administrator changes. Which option is most defensible after weighing security value, operational burden, and evidence quality?

choices.A: Enable tamper protection, privileged elevation control, health monitoring, and alerting on telemetry gaps
choices.B: Investigate software inventory drift, remote access exposure, approval evidence, and persistence behavior
choices.C: Use application allowlisting with change control, exception handling, and monitoring
choices.D: Require MDM posture controls, encryption, lock policy, compliance checks, and conditional access
choices.E: Tie patch/configuration compliance to risk-based exceptions, owners, due dates, and compensating controls

normalQuestions.explanation: Reliable endpoint security depends on telemetry the agent can deliver and on limiting who can disable it. The defensible package enables tamper protection, controls privileged elevation, monitors agent health, and alerts on telemetry gaps, directly addressing telemetry lost after local-admin changes. Surface investigation, allowlisting, MDM, and patch governance solve adjacent problems instead.

whyWrong.B: Surface investigation fits unexpected tools on endpoints, not protecting telemetry.
whyWrong.C: Allowlisting controls execution, not agent telemetry reliability.
whyWrong.D: MDM posture fits mobile device compliance, not server telemetry integrity.
whyWrong.E: Patch and exception governance manages vulnerability risk, not telemetry loss.

sources: CAS005 LO 3.2: Given a scenario, analyze requirements to enhance the security of endpoints and servers.

whyCorrect.A: Tamper protection, elevation control, and telemetry-gap alerting keep the agent reporting despite local-admin changes.

normalQuestions.learningObjective: Given a scenario, apply threat-hunting and threat intelligence concepts.
normalQuestions.stem: Hunters want to query a suspected attacker-infrastructure domain directly from corporate IP space. A program owner needs a recommendation defensible to legal, audit, and engineering. Which elements belong in the design package? (Select all that apply.)

choices.A: Avoid direct beaconing
choices.B: Map fields
choices.C: Document handling
choices.D: Use controlled research paths
choices.E: Create detections

normalQuestions.explanation: Querying adversary infrastructure from corporate IPs can warn the attacker they have been spotted. Counterintelligence and OPSEC require avoiding direct contact that beacons interest (A), documenting how findings are handled (C), and researching through controlled paths (D). Mapping detection fields and creating detections are detection-engineering tasks, not OPSEC controls.

whyWrong.B: Mapping fields supports portable detection logic, not OPSEC research.
whyWrong.E: Creating detections is detection engineering, not research safety.

sources: CAS005 LO 4.3: Given a scenario, apply threat-hunting and threat intelligence concepts.

whyCorrect.A: Avoiding direct beaconing keeps the adversary from learning they are under investigation.
whyCorrect.C: Documenting handling keeps sensitive research controlled and auditable.
whyCorrect.D: Controlled research paths prevent corporate IPs from exposing defender interest.

normalQuestions.learningObjective: Given a scenario, analyze vulnerabilities and attacks, and recommend solutions to reduce the attack surface.
normalQuestions.stem: A program owner needs a recommendation that can be defended to legal, audit, and engineering. The team already bought tooling, but the unresolved issue is that a legacy service parses untrusted files inside a privileged process. Which elements belong in the design package? (Select all that apply.)

choices.A: Drop privileges
choices.B: Deny metadata endpoints
choices.C: Sandbox process
choices.D: Restrict egress
choices.E: Patch parser

normalQuestions.explanation: Parsing untrusted input in a privileged process risks attacker code running with high privilege. The fix needs both containment and code-level controls: drop privileges (A), sandbox the process (C), and patch the parser (E). Denying metadata endpoints and restricting egress are SSRF controls, not defenses for a privileged parser.

whyWrong.B: Denying metadata endpoints is an SSRF control, not a parsing defense.
whyWrong.D: Restricting egress counters SSRF, not untrusted-file parsing.

sources: CAS005 LO 4.2: Given a scenario, analyze vulnerabilities and attacks, and recommend solutions to reduce the attack surface.

whyCorrect.A: Dropping privileges limits the damage if the parser is exploited.
whyCorrect.C: Sandboxing contains a parser exploit away from the rest of the system.
whyCorrect.E: Patching the parser removes the underlying memory/execution flaw.

normalQuestions.learningObjective: Given a scenario, integrate Zero Trust concepts into system architecture design.
normalQuestions.stem: A security council is deciding which evidence to require before approval. The debate started when auditors asked for proof, since compromising one workload lets the attacker reach unrelated databases. Which items best distinguish a defensible answer from a superficial one? (Select all that apply.)

choices.A: Authorize object access
choices.B: Verify device posture
choices.C: Monitor east-west flows
choices.D: Define service policies
choices.E: Deny by default

normalQuestions.explanation: Zero Trust limits lateral movement by narrowing trust relationships between systems. To prove a compromised workload cannot reach unrelated databases, the design monitors east-west (service-to-service) flows (C), defines explicit service policies (D), and denies by default (E). Authorizing object access (A) is about verifying internal calls, and verifying device posture (B) is asset attestation; neither directly contains lateral movement.

whyWrong.A: Authorizing object access verifies internal requests, but does not segment workloads from each other.
whyWrong.B: Verifying device posture is asset attestation, not workload segmentation.

sources: CAS005 LO 2.6: Given a scenario, integrate Zero Trust concepts into system architecture design.

whyCorrect.C: Monitoring east-west flows reveals and controls service-to-service traffic that enables lateral movement.
whyCorrect.D: Defining service policies sets which services may talk to which, narrowing trust.
whyCorrect.E: Denying by default blocks any unapproved path between workloads.

Approved data classes, with redaction and retention rules
Don't log AI use at all

fields.label: Controller zone

pbqs.title: Threat Hunt From Intelligence

correct: New scheduled tasks created by unusual accounts

pbqs.title: Resilient System Design Review
pbqs.scenario: An order platform has a 20-minute RTO and a 5-minute RPO. The web tier spans multiple zones, the database replicates asynchronously, the message broker has no tested restore, and backups can be changed by platform admins.

fields.label: Primary RPO gap
options: The web tier has two zones but no independent data objective
Asynchronous replication may lose more than 5 minutes of data
Dashboard display settings changed during the outage
fields.correct: Asynchronous replication may lose more than 5 minutes of data
fields.explanation: RPO is about how much data loss is acceptable; async replication can exceed that 5-minute limit.

fields.label: Evidence required
fields.explanation: Resilience claims must be backed by tested dependencies and recovery evidence, not just a diagram.

fields.label: Backup integrity control
options: Mutable backups managed by the same admins
Immutable backups with separated admin duties
fields.correct: Immutable backups with separated admin duties
fields.explanation: Backup integrity is what lets you recover after a destructive incident.

fields.label: Incident recovery action order
options: Fix the root cause and update detections
correct: Fix the root cause and update detections
fields.explanation: The response sequence preserves evidence, limits damage, eradicates the root cause, and then proves the restore is clean — restoring before the root cause is fixed risks immediate re-compromise.

fields.label: IR/recovery coordination
options: Fix the root cause before resuming normal operation
correct: Fix the root cause before resuming normal operation
fields.explanation: Incident recovery should preserve evidence and prevent the issue from recurring.

keywords.text: Immutable backups with separated admin duties
